docs.title: GPU-Accelerated Virtual Flume Lab
docs.text:
SPH-based wave tank campaigns in DualSPHysics, with expert support for case set-up, model optimization, and validation, executed on a multi-GPU node and delivered as calibrated time series, field outputs, and technical reports.

Request lab time Test programmes

docs.title: Test programmes
docs.text:
• Wave energy converters

    Floating and bottom-referenced WECs with multibody constraints and power take-off models through the Project Chrono library, moored with MoorDynPlus.

    Outputs include 6-DoF motions per body, power take-off force and velocity, absorbed power, capture width ratio and RAOs.

  • Breaking waves on monopiles

    Wave transformation in highly energetic state, including their impact on fixed or moored structures, such as monopiles or floating platform.

    Outputs include slamming and inline forces, local impact pressures and run-up.

  • Focused waves on moored structures

    NewWave-type focused wave groups with prescribed focus location and time, applied to fixed or moored floating bodies.

    Outputs include peak motions, vibration amplitude, mooring tensions with snap loads, and green water.

  • Multisine tests

    Broadband multisine excitation with Schroeder or crest-factor-optimised phases for linear system identification.

    Outputs include transfer functions \(H(f) = S_{xy}/S_{xx}\), coherence and RAOs.

docs.title: About the lab
docs.text:
A virtual laboratory for GPU-accelerated hydrodynamics, operated by researchers who develop and apply SPH methods.

Physical wave flumes and basins are, in principle, expensive to operate and require long turn over to operate. GPU-accelerated meshless methods now make it possible to reproduce many of these tests numerically, at resolutions and durations that were previously impractical. This lab maintains and verifies numerical wave tanks and commits to dedicated multi-GPU node, in addition to providing the expertise to set up, optimize, and validate the models; our effort should then let academic and industrial users obtain dependable data without building the infrastructure themselves.

docs.title: Estimation model
docs.text:
The fluid particle count follows from the water volume and the particle spacing, increased by the boundary overhead.

\[ N_{3D} = \frac{L\,W\,d}{dp^3}, \qquad N_{2D} = \frac{L\,d}{dp^2} \]

The speed of sound is scaled from the dam-break velocity, and the time step is limited by the CFL condition on the smoothing length, with \(n_d\) the number of dimensions.

\[ c_0 = \text{coefsound}\,\sqrt{g\,d}, \qquad h_s = \text{coefh}\,\sqrt{n_d}\,dp, \qquad \Delta t = \text{CFL}\,\frac{h_s}{c_0} \]

The wall-clock time is the number of steps times the cost per step, divided by the effective number of GPUs.

\[ t_{wall} = \frac{t_{sim}}{\Delta t}\cdot\frac{N\,\tau_p}{n_{GPU}\,\varepsilon} \]

Here \(\tau_p\) is the measured cost per particle per step on one GPU and \(\varepsilon\) the parallel efficiency, taken as 1 for a single GPU. The estimate excludes output writing, floating-body and mooring coupling, and post-processing, and assumes the time step stays close to its acoustic limit. The values are indicative and are refined during scoping with a short benchmark of the actual case.

docs.title: Cost scaling
docs.text:
For a 3-D WCSPH model, the particle count scales as \(N \propto dp^{-3}\) and the time step, limited by the CFL condition, as \(\Delta t \propto h/c_0 \propto dp\). The cost of a run for a fixed simulated time therefore scales approximately as

\[ \text{cost} \propto N \cdot \frac{t_{sim}}{\Delta t} \propto dp^{-4}. \]

Halving \(dp\) increases the cost by about a factor of 16 in 3D and 8 in 2D. This is why the facility offers a trade-off between resolution and duration rather than both at once, and why the convergence study is done before production.

Estimate the run time of your model

docs.title: Allocation policy
docs.text:
• Facility time is allocated in windows, as in a physical laboratory. Window length and run configuration are fixed during scoping.
  • Models are optimised with the lab team before the window opens, so allocated time is used for production runs.
  • Allocations are time-limited to keep the facility available to academic and industrial users.

docs.title: Services
docs.text: Each service combines access to the numerical infrastructure with direct support from people who develop and validate SPH models. Services can be booked separately or combined into a full test campaign.

docs.title: Numerical wave tank campaigns
docs.text:
A preconfigured and verified wave tank in DualSPHysics (weakly compressible SPH). Users supply the structure or device and the test matrix; we implement it in the tank.

  • Implementation of fixed, floating and moored bodies from CAD (STL/OBJ) or parametric definitions.
  • Regular, irregular, focused, solitary and multisine wave conditions, at model or prototype scale under Froude similarity.
  • Instrumentation matched to the quantities of interest, including free-surface gauges, pressure and velocity probes, integrated forces and moments, and rigid-body kinematics.

See the wave tank specification.

docs.title: Model development and optimisation
docs.text:
• Selection of particle spacing \(dp\) based on wave height, wavelength and the smallest relevant geometric scale.
  • Choice of boundary formulation (mDBC), density diffusion (δ-SPH) and viscosity model (artificial or laminar + SPS).
  • Tuning of wavemaker transfer functions, active absorption and damping-zone length to minimise reflection.
  • Code-level support for users running their own GPU solvers on the node.

docs.title: Verification and validation
docs.text:
• Convergence studies on \(dp\), with quantified sensitivity of the target quantities.
  • Verification of wave generation against the target spectrum, \(H_{m0} = 4\sqrt{m_0}\) and \(T_p\), with reflection analysis by the Mansard and Funke three-gauge method.
  • Validation against analytical solutions, published benchmarks or user-supplied experimental data, with error metrics such as normalised RMSE and phase error.

docs.title: GPU facility allocation
docs.text: Time-boxed access to a node with 10 × NVIDIA L40S, configured either as a single multi-GPU simulation or as parallel runs. See the facility page and the run-time estimator.

docs.title: Data and reporting
docs.text:
• Raw time series (CSV) and field output (VTK) organised per run, with metadata describing case parameters and solver settings.
  • Post-processing with spectral analysis, exceedance statistics, transfer functions, RAOs, load and pressure statistics, and animations.
  • A technical report covering set-up, numerical parameters, verification, validation and results, when required.

Request lab time

docs.title: Numerical wave tank
docs.text: A verified 2D flume and 3D tank implemented in DualSPHysics, a GPU-accelerated weakly compressible SPH (WCSPH) solver. The tank is supplied ready for testing; the user's structure, device and test matrix are implemented during set-up.

docs.title: Facility sheet
docs.text:
Values describe the default configuration. Domain dimensions, water depth, bathymetry and instrumentation are adapted to each campaign during scoping.

Item Specification Solver DualSPHysics, WCSPH on GPU (CUDA) Configurations 2-D flume; 3-D tank or basin Wavemakers Piston and flap; first-order and second-order (Madsen) generation Wave conditions Regular, irregular (JONSWAP, Pierson–Moskowitz), focused, solitary, multisine, user-defined paddle signals Absorption Active wave absorption at the paddle (AWAS); passive damping zones; optional open boundaries Rigid bodies 6-DoF floating bodies; constraints, joints and linear springs, or dampers via Project Chrono Moorings Lumped-mass mooring lines via MoorDyn+ Instruments Free-surface gauges, pressure and velocity probes, integrated forces and moments, body kinematics Outputs CSV time series; VTK particle and iso-surface fields for ParaView

docs.title: Wave generation and absorption
docs.text: Paddle motion is derived from the Biésel transfer function for the target wave field, with second-order correction to suppress spurious free long waves where required. Irregular sea states are synthesised from the target spectrum; focused waves use NewWave-type groups with prescribed focus time and location. Reflection is controlled by active absorption at the paddle and passive damping at the far end, and checked with three-gauge reflection analysis. In addition, customized free-surface elevation can be used to command the motion of the piston or flap generator.

docs.title: Resolution guidance
docs.text:
Criterion Typical starting point Particles per wave height, \(H/dp\) ≥ 8 for propagation; finer for breaking and impact Particles across the smallest body dimension Set by the load or motion of interest, and confirmed by convergence Damping zone length ≥ 1–2 wavelengths Smoothing length \(h = 1.3\times \text{coefh}\,\sqrt{d}\,dp\), with \(d\) the number of dimensions

Final values are confirmed by convergence studies on the quantities that matter for the campaign.

docs.title: Required material
docs.text:
• Geometry (STL/OBJ, or a drawing with dimensions), mass properties for floating bodies, and mooring layout if relevant.
  • The test matrix, specifying wave conditions, water depth, scale, and duration of each run.
  • The quantities to be measured and their required accuracy.
  • Experimental or reference data for validation, if available.
  • A preliminary working model, for example built from our downloadable tanks.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
The facility is open to academic and industrial users under two access routes. Both require a motivated request, defined expected results and a preliminary working model.

  • Researchers and students

    Research groups, PhD candidates and MSc/BSc students at universities and research institutes. Requests are assessed on scientific merit, need for the facility and model readiness.

    Academic access

  • Companies and SMEs

    Benchmarking and validation campaigns with priority scheduling, confidentiality and full campaign support from the lab team.

    Industry access

The steps of a campaign are the same for both routes; see the campaign workflow.

docs.title: Access for companies
docs.text: For companies and SMEs that need to benchmark a design or validate a specific numerical model. Industrial users receive privileged access to the facility and a team that runs the campaign from set-up to technical report.

docs.title: Typical engagements
docs.text:
• Benchmarking a device or structure across a defined test matrix of regular, irregular or focused wave conditions.
  • Validating a proprietary numerical model (potential-flow, CFD or reduced-order) against high-fidelity SPH results, or validating the SPH model against the client's experimental data.
  • Comparing design variants under identical wave conditions.
  • Extreme-event assessment with focused wave groups, and impact loads from breaking waves.

docs.title: Privileged access
docs.text: Scheduling Priority allocation windows booked around the project timeline Confidentiality Non-disclosure agreement and data ownership terms agreed before any model is shared Support Set-up, optimisation, verification, validation, production runs and analysis by the lab team Reporting Technical report covering set-up, numerical parameters, verification, validation and results

docs.title: Required material
docs.text:
• A statement of the engineering question and how the results will be used, so the test matrix answers it.
  • A preliminary model of the device or structure. Where only a design exists, geometry, mass properties and key parameters are sufficient, and building the numerical model becomes part of the engagement.
  • Experimental or reference data, if the campaign includes validation.

Each engagement is scoped and quoted individually.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Complete data set from every run, organised and documented.
  • Processed results for loads, pressures, motions, mooring tensions, transfer functions and RAOs.
  • Technical report, ready for internal or external use.

Request a scoping call

docs.title: Access for researchers and students
docs.text: For scientists, research groups and students at universities and research institutes. Allocations are granted to projects that justify the use of the facility, state their expected results and arrive with a model that already runs.

docs.title: Eligibility
docs.text:
• Researchers and scientists at universities and research institutes.
  • PhD candidates, for thesis work.
  • MSc and BSc students, with the supervisor named in the request and copied on correspondence.

docs.title: Request contents
docs.text:
Motivation Justification for the facility, such as resolution, domain size or simulated duration beyond local resources, or tests that are impractical in a physical tank. Expected results Target quantities and required accuracy, the proposed test matrix, and the intended output, whether a thesis chapter, journal paper or project deliverable. Preliminary working model A case that runs end to end, even at coarse \(dp\) or in 2D, with evidence that it produces physically reasonable results. The 2D and 3D tanks are a suitable starting point.

A proposal template is available.

docs.title: Assessment criteria
docs.text:
Criterion Assessment basis Need for the facility The case cannot reasonably run on local resources, or the facility substantially improves resolution or statistics Clarity of expected results Defined quantities of interest, test matrix and validation strategy Model readiness A working preliminary model that can be scaled to production resolution Feasibility The campaign fits within an allocation window

Requests that are promising but not ready receive feedback on what is missing.

docs.title: Provided support
docs.text:
• Support implementing the case in the wave tank.
  • Model optimisation, covering \(dp\) selection, numerical settings and a convergence study.
  • An allocation window in the run configuration that suits the model.
  • Organised data with metadata, and a methods description suitable for citation.
